The cornea is depicted as the transparent curved front surface that refracts incoming light rays. Behind the cornea lies the anterior chamber filled with aqueous humor. The iris surrounds the pupil which controls light entry. The lens sits posterior to the iris and adjusts its shape for focusing. The vitreous humor fills the large central chamber of the eye. The retina lines the inner back wall and contains millions of photoreceptor cells including rod cells for low-light vision distributed across the peripheral retina and cone cells concentrated in the central area for color vision and detail. The optic disk marks where the optic nerve exits the eye, appearing as a circular structure. The optic nerve bundle transmits electrical signals from retinal ganglion cells to the brain for visual processing. The sclera forms the white outer fibrous layer providing structural support. The choroid layer beneath the retina supplies blood and nutrients. All structures are shown in cross-sectional view with accurate spatial relationships and layering.
